CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Treat Trump’s August 1 List 4 announcement as a breach of the Osaka pause and keep the proportional response already launched: the halt of U.S. farm purchases, the option of extra tariffs on post-August 3 ag shipments, and a market-driven yuan above 7. Do not resume agricultural buying or offer structural concessions until List 4 is withdrawn or clearly deferred. Hold rare-earth export controls and the unreliable-entity list in reserve rather than firing them before September 1, and stay available for the planned Washington round without new commitments.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. Combined U.S. Section 301 coverage is already ~$250B at 25% (List 3 hiked May 10), Huawei remains on the Entity List with Google/chip-supply cuts (May 16–20), and List 4 would put 10% duties on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods from September 1—effectively the entire bilateral export book. That lands on an economy already growing 6.2% in Q2, the slowest quarterly pace in 27 years, with H1 exports to the U.S. down 8.1% and June factory jobs shedding at the fastest pace since the global crisis. The August 5 break of 7 CNY/USD and the first U.S. currency-manipulator designation since 1994 add FX and financial-stability pressure. This is the +0.5 CHN anchor (major export hit, FX pressure, firm-level tech targeting), not +1.0: growth is still inside the 6–6.5% target, stimulus capacity remains, List 4 is not yet in force, and the manipulator label is largely symbolic for a year. Action should stay retaliatory rather than concessional or maximally escalatory. MOFCOM/Xinhua already called List 4 a “serious violation” of the June 29 Osaka understanding (no new tariffs “for the time being”) and suspended farm purchases—the scarce lever that actually bites U.S. politics. Folding back into purchases now would reward a post-Shanghai surprise after talks produced “little progress.” Further non-tariff escalation (implementing the May 31 unreliable-entity list or converting Xi’s May 20 rare-earth signal into an embargo) would invite a still-harsher U.S. response while China’s own growth is already soft. U.S. markets are signaling pain too (10-year yield 1.71% on August 7, −35% in the window; Fed already cut in July), so holding the farm halt and keeping September talks open without new text is enough leverage through the September 1 window.
key_factors: List 4 (10% on remaining ~$300B) announced Aug 1, effective Sept 1, after Osaka 'no new tariffs' pause
Huawei still on Entity List; Android/GMS and U.S. chip supply already cut
Q2 GDP 6.2% — 27-year low; H1 exports to U.S. -8.1%
CNY through 7 and first U.S. manipulator designation since 1994
Farm-purchase halt already launched as the main political counter-lever
September Washington talks still on the calendar; List 4 not yet in force

sources_cited.excerpt: After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs "for the time being."
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
List 3 tariff rate rises from 10% to 25%.
Trade talks in Shanghai (through July 31). Little progress reported.
U.S. 10-year Treasury yield latest 1.71 on 2019-08-07, change -0.94 (-35.5%) over the window.
China's economy grew 6.2% in the second quarter... the country's slowest pace since the first quarter of 1992.
China’s exports to the United States decreased 8.1% for the first six months of 2019. Imports from the United States plunged 30% year on year.
China “has not ruled out import tariffs on US agricultural products purchased after August 3, and related Chinese companies have suspended purchasing US agricultural products."
The president’s decision last week to impose a new 10 percent tariff on $300 billion worth of Chinese goods was “a serious violation” of the agreement between Trump and Xi at Osaka.
